newsitem.title: GERMANY: INSTANT VIEW - German unemployment data for June.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - German unemployment data for June.

text.p: Following are economists' reactions to a report from the Federal Labour Office showing the seasonally adjusted jobless total rose by 11,000 in June from May. They spoke with Reuters Financial Television.

Guenther Redeker, Chase Investment, London: The cut in the labour-providing programme for east Germany did some harm. We have seen a relatively large loss in construction jobs in east Germany. The three month average for this time of the year are worse than last year. The worst in the labour market is not over yet. Why is unemployment still rising? Investment is still declining. We have to assume that the labour market will remain depressed in the absence of any investment activity.

Assuming that our forecast is correct that the labour market is worsening this year, Mr Waigel's budget is under pressure again. Under the (government) tax estimation, they see a relationship between gradual economic growth and tax proceeds, but this may not be true. I guess that Mr Waigel is not out of the woods."

Ulrich Beckmann, Senior Economist, Deutsche Bank Research: "They are very close to our forecast, but a little bit on the disappointing side. I would assume that the increase is based on east Germany. It is to be seen against the cutting of costs in job creation schemes. I expect a slight improvement this year and for 1998, but it will be a very very slight improvement.
Mr Waigel is trying very hard (to meet Maastricht deficit goals). This number is neutral in terms of impact on the budget figure. Our foreaset is for a 3.2 percent (of GDP) deficit."

Thomas Hueck, Economist, Bayerische Vereinsbank, Munich: "We see in the east German economy a technical reason for the reduction in job incentive schemes which mostly hit the construction sector. The labour market doesn't make it easier for Mr Waigel. The tax estimates from this spring are very comfortable. They had a safety margin. I think Waigel will make three percent."
